messages:
maria: Heads-up — a quick follow-up from yesterday's RFC review about the UI data layer and authz checks.
maria: TL;DR: Proposal is to move most RBAC enforcement out of the query-service and into the API gateway + fronting cache. want to list tradeoffs & a rollout plan.
ajay: ok, why move it upstream? what about duplication of logic across gateways/private deployments?
maria: main reason is latency and simpler query-service contracts. Right now query-service fetches full datasets and then filters for perms which is expensive for big panels. Upstream checks let us short-circuit and serve cached per-principal views.
samir: downside is duplicated policy code + risk of divergent behavior. Also harder for Dedicated / Private where customers may want policy in their networks.
katie: can we make a small interface: query-service accepts an "authz token" that proves gateway evaluated perms? then query-service trusts that and skips per-row filtering.
leo: that seems reasonable, but we need a cryptographic proof (signed token) and an expiry window. otherwise it's a security hole.
maria: agreed. idea: gateway signs a JWT with claims {sub:user, org, allowed_filters, exp, sig}. query-service verifies signature using key published in config/KMS. For private deployments KMS/key is customer-managed.
ajay: sounds good. still worried about worst-case: gateway lies or bug; defense-in-depth suggests query-service should keep a cheap fallback check for sensitive resources.
samir: cheap fallback = validate resource-level ACL checks only (e.g., org-level, dataset-level) rather than per-row evaluation. saves CPU but keeps last-resort guard.
katie: also we should keep a sampling mode for full enforcement for telemetry. every 1% of requests do full-per-row enforcement and log diffs.
leo: +1 for sampling. we can store sampling traces in the perf infra and tie to traces.
infra-bot: deploy-note: when adding JWT verify step, add a new env var QUERY_TRUSTED_KEYS and feature flag: feature.authz_jwt_enabled
maria: caching idea: cache per-panel responses keyed by (org, panel_id, authz_hash, query_sig). authz_hash = hash(allowed_filters + user_roles). That way panels with same perms share cache.
ajay: watch cache cardinality — per-user caching will explode. we should prefer per-org or per-role caches and only enable per-user for small panels.
samir: agree. propose cache tiers: global shared cache for public panels, org-level for org-wide views, user-level only for tiny widgets.
katie: what about multi-tenant Dedicated where a customer pins a model and has heavy dashboards? we should allow customers to set cache QPS quotas and invalidation hooks.
leo: invalidation hooks: add endpoints to purge panel cache by panel_id/org via service account. Also support TTL and manual flush from console.
maria: perf numbers we discussed: e2e median for big table widget is ~1800ms currently, most of that is scanning/permission filtering. With upstream authz + org-level cache we can target 250-400ms.
ajay: nice but what about cold cache misses and burst traffic? we should do pre-warm for scheduled dashboards and stagger refreshes.
katie: and add circuit-breaker: if query-service latency > 1.2s for panel, fallback to a degraded view: "cached snapshot" with timestamp + notice.
samir: important for SLAs. Also make sure we surface metrics: authz_verification_latency, cache_hit_rate_by_tier, fallback_rate.
leo: instrumentation plan: add trace tag authz.source=(gateway|local), authz.signed=true/false, cache.tier, cache.key_hash. then alert on authz.signed=false for prod.
maria: rollout plan:
- phase 0 (canary): add JWT verify code but keep local enforcement enabled. feature flag off. sample 0.1% full compare logs.
- phase 1: enable authz_jwt_enabled behind feature flag for 10% traffic in prod, still run local check but cheap.
- phase 2: flip to trust JWT for non-sensitive panels (config whitelist), enable org-level cache.
- phase 3: expand to more panels + per-role caches, expose cache controls in console.
- phase 4: private/dedicated: expose key config + allow customers to opt into local-only enforcement.

maria: action items:
- @ajay: design JWT claim set + key rotation policy (owner: ajay) (ETA 2w)
- @samir: implement cheap fallback ACL checks + sampling compare (owner: samir) (ETA 3w)
- @leo: cache tiers + purge API + instrumentation (owner: leo) (ETA 3w)
- @katie: update console controls and add UI for cache TTL + manual purge (owner: katie) (ETA 4w)
- infra-bot: create feature flag feature.authz_jwt_enabled in FF service

ajay: question — what do we consider "sensitive" panels? should be a panel property flagged by product teams.
maria: yes, add metadata on panel: sensitivity: public|org|sensitive. Sensitive panels always run local per-row enforce.
samir: and policy for evaluations: keep eval suites for these panels to ensure no divergence.
katie: docs note: console docs should include recommended cache configs per widget type.
leo: security note: key rotation must be seamless — JWTs short TTL (30s) and rotate keys with old keys kept for overlap.
infra-bot: ci-note: add unit tests for JWT verify and integration test that injects a gateway-signed token.
maria: OK let's sync on Wed for blockers. I'm going to update the RFC doc with the contract + sample JWT payload.
ajay: thanks — appreciate the concrete plan.
samir: happy with sampling approach.
katie: will prototype console ttl controls next sprint.
leo: will sketch cache design in arch doc.
maria: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
